title: Dr. Jazz requests, invitation to Rome, Washington ball and Historical Society record
summary: Crowds wanted Dr. Jazz, which the band did not know. Upcoming: Rome, a Congressional Carnival Ball and a recording for a Louisiana society.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: What tunes did they request most often?

Every time we would play, we'd have a hundred requests for Dr. Jazz. And unfortunately, the lead man didn't know Dr. Jazz. I know it now, though. And if ever, oh, we got a letter. They just sent us a letter. They want us to go to Rome next year for a similar DLC. And you can bet if we go to Rome, I will play Dr. Jazz until I'm blue in the face. I know it now.

I have to give you that guy's name over there that I know. His name is Claude Cock. K-O-C-H. He sounds like a Frenchman and a German, but he's in Rome last I heard from him. He was over here in Biloxi training for the Italian Air Force. And he bought a lot of my records. He wanted to get old, you know, kid shots records and stuff like that. I was starving, I think, at the time. I told him, $30 worth of records.

Well, we got this letter. I mean, they want us to go to Rome now. Well, it's going to be a similar deal. And we also supposed to go to Washington, D.C., February 27th for the, they got this Congressional Carnival Ball over there. And we supposed to play for that. So we keep an active just enough to, you know, keep in shape, you know. Do you rehearse? Huh? Do you rehearse? Well, I'll tell you, there's rumor that we're getting ready to make a record for the Louisiana Historical Society. Now, this, this fella made a contact with us. He figured that our groups still sound like one of the real old, original New Orleans bands. So that's why he decided on using our groups. And they want to, they want us to record, I think it's something like 12 tunes. And we have been rehearsing this past week. We're going to start rehearsals so we can get these tunes down to the note, you know, so there will be no flaws.
It contacts through Bill Cray, you know. I didn't know that. I didn't know that.
Yeah, he's the one that tipped him off. Really?
It's the Louisiana Folklore Society. Is that what it is?

Well, I tell you, there's business going over my head all the time. I just know that I should show up when we have an engagement. Yeah. I'll leave all the figure into Chaff and Ice. They have been making most of the arrangements for us and whatnot. But I just work for the bunch, you know.
Yeah, Bill used to sit in too. He's in that one. Bill Cray, yeah. He did sit in already, yeah. Raymond played a few jobs, you see.
